data.title: Reset & Revert
data.tagline: Reset moves the current branch and handles changes by mode; revert adds a commit that offsets an earlier change
data.description: Suppose B adjusts navigation and C accidentally adds a debug entry. If C is only local, reset can move the branch pointer; --soft keeps changes staged, the default --mixed resets the index but leaves working-tree files, and --hard also replaces tracked working-tree files. If C is on a shared branch and teammates may have based work on it, revert usually appends a commit that offsets C while preserving later history. If later edits overlap with C, revert may also require conflict resolution.

use: For an unshared commit, consider reset only after checking staged and working-tree changes
Keep changes but redo the commit with --soft
For a shared commit, consider revert and check for conflicts
Before --hard, inspect tracked-file changes it will replace in the index and working tree
avoid: Reset a shared branch and force push without coordinating with teammates
Run reset --hard without checking which tracked-file changes it will replace
Revert without reviewing later edits that may overlap and need conflict resolution
scenarios: Local commits B and C, including a debug entry
Reset --soft moves the branch but keeps staged changes
Revert appends an offsetting commit to shared history
Recheck navigation and teammate changes remain

lessonPractice.title: Commit C added a debug entry and was shared; a teammate later made commit D. How can you offset C and keep D?

options.label: Review C and D, use git revert C to append an offsetting commit, then check the result
options.feedback: Correct. Revert appends a commit to the current history; inspect the new diff to confirm it offsets only C and keeps B and D. Resolve any overlapping edits before verifying.

options.label: Reset to before C and force push, removing C and later commit D
options.feedback: That rewrites history teammates may already use and also removes D from the branch line.

options.label: Run git revert HEAD to undo the latest commit D, then push
options.feedback: HEAD points to the teammate's later D; reverting it removes the help update while leaving debug entry C. Name the commit you intend to offset.

data.agentPrompt: Commit C accidentally added a debug entry, and a teammate later made D. Review the diffs for C and D, then use git revert C to append an offsetting commit. Explain possible conflicts and only resolve the parts related to C. Confirm B’s navigation and D’s content remain, the debug entry is gone, rerun the page, and tell me the new commit hash.
